qa.q: May one eat chicken with milk?

paras.text: No. Eating poultry with milk is forbidden by rabbinic decree, though not by the Torah.
Unlike meat with milk, cooking poultry with milk or benefiting from it is not forbidden; only eating it is.

sources.title: Mishneh Torah, Forbidden Foods 9
sources.note: The Rambam on meat and milk, poultry included.

sources.title: Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 87
sources.note: Which meat and milk are forbidden to cook, eat and benefit from.

qa.q: How long after meat before dairy?

paras.text: The common practice is to wait six hours.
Some communities keep shorter customs, recorded by the Rema. Ask your rabbi which custom your family follows.

sources.title: Mishneh Torah, Forbidden Foods 9:28
sources.note: Waiting after meat before eating dairy.

sources.title: Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 89:1
sources.note: Six hours, with the Rema on other customs.

qa.q: Does the app work on Shabbat?

paras.text: From candle lighting to Havdalah the app works from saved data and sends nothing to the network.

how.title: The camera reads the barcode
how.text: EAN-13, EAN-8 or UPC-E, the codes on packages in stores. This already works in the app.

how.title: We look it up in connected lists
how.text: Each list is kept separately, with the organization’s name and the edition.

how.title: Whole product lines count
how.text: If your list says “all plain yogurts of brand X”, the scanner matches the brand and category and shows your wording verbatim.

how.title: Every answer is signed
how.text: Organization, list edition and markings: dairy, pareve, Pesach. The app does not rule on kashrut.

how.title: Honest when it doesn’t know
how.text: “Not found” does not mean “not kosher”, and the scanner says so. If a product left the new edition, it says that too.

how.title: Silent on Shabbat
how.text: From candle lighting to Havdalah the app does not go online, and neither does the scanner.

steps.title: You send the list
steps.text: A spreadsheet or a PDF, whichever is easier.

steps.title: We digitize it
steps.text: Every row is checked against the original.

steps.title: We link barcodes
steps.text: A person checks every uncertain match.

steps.title: You review
steps.text: Nothing is published without your confirmation.

steps.title: Your list is live
steps.text: We update to a new edition when you tell us.

gets.title: Your list works at the shelf
gets.text: A PDF is hard to read in a store. The scanner answers in a second, and shoppers see the answer came from you.

gets.title: Feedback
gets.text: Error reports and anonymized statistics: which products people look for and do not find.

gets.title: Alerts about suspicious marks
gets.text: Users will be able to send a photo of a mark that does not match yours. We will pass it on to you.

partners.terms_h2: You remain the source and the owner of your list
terms: Published only after you check it.
Every entry names your organization and the list edition.
Any entry, or the whole list, is removed on request.
Your kashrut mark is shown only with your permission.

faq.q: Will you decide what is kosher?
faq.a: No. The app shows one thing only: the product is on the list of a given organization, in a given edition, with given markings. The person and their rabbi decide.
Every entry names its organization, and users choose which organizations they trust. We do not rank organizations.

faq.q: We already have our own app.
faq.a: We can show your list with a link to your app, or simply exchange data. Whatever works for you.
The scanner in the app reads barcodes and shows the product name and maker. We are starting to connect organizations’ lists now, and you can be among the first.

partners.contact_lead: Write to us and we will get in touch. You can tell us about your list right away: how many products it has and in what format.
